subject: Governing law + injunctive relief: proposed compromise for tribunal scope
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@stormcommerce.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 03 Nov 2028 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: MSA redlines and jurisdiction concerns

Hi Laura,

Thanks again for the call yesterday. Attached are our redlines to the MSA (StormCommerce_MSA_redlines_20281102.pdf) and a short one-pager summarizing our legal team's open items. Two headline items: governing law (we prefer New York law) and an explicit forum for injunctive relief; your draft points to Delaware and a broad arbitration requirement.

Our commercial team is OK with arbitration for most disputes, but StormCommerce needs clarity that we can seek emergency injunctive relief in New York courts (our primary HQ) without being forced to arbitrate first. We also asked for a limited carveout for equitable relief where injunctive relief is necessary to preserve customer data or stop ongoing unauthorized access.

Can Redwood confirm whether you will accept: 1) Delaware law as governing, with 2) an exception allowing either party to seek interim injunctive relief in New York state or federal court, limited to preservation/emergency measures, and 3) an agreement that arbitration will proceed for the substantive claims after any interim measure? If not, please tell us the alternative language you can accept.

We have a procurement timeline target of Thanksgiving week and need final MSA language to route to our VP Legal. If you can provide proposed language today, we can accelerate.

Attachments:
- StormCommerce_MSA_redlines_20281102.pdf (redline)
- security-supplement-ask.pdf (list of evidence requests)

Thanks,

Elena Ruiz
General Counsel
StormCommerce

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@stormcommerce.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 03 Nov 2028 10:05:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: MSA redlines and jurisdiction concerns

Elena —

Thanks for the redlines and the clear ask. We want to keep the MSA clean for our platform customers, but we also recognize the practical need for an interim relief carveout. High level: Redwood is willing to propose a narrowly tailored compromise that preserves our arbitration-first model while allowing emergency equitable relief in the customer's local courts. Suggested approach below.

Proposal (we can add to the redline):
- Governing law: Delaware (state) — stays as-is for consistency across the Redwood MSA.
- Injunctive/Equitable relief carveout: either party may seek interim injunctive or other provisional relief in a court of competent jurisdiction located in the claimant's principal place of business (e.g., New York for StormCommerce) for the limited purpose of preserving the status quo, preventing data exfiltration, or protecting confidential information.
- Arbitration sequencing: any interim court action does not waive the right to arbitrate the underlying dispute; arbitration proceeds on the merits once interim measures are sought/obtained.
- Scope limits: carveout limited to emergency relief (preservation, urgent confidentiality/data protection) and expressly excludes damages claims and declarations beyond immediate preservation.

Next steps: if StormCommerce accepts the approach, I will produce a short redline with the exact contract language and circulate for signatures. Jonas/Marissa — see below for operational/commercial concerns and any tweaks you want to add to the draft language.

Laura Bennett
Senior Contracts Counsel | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com | +1-415-555-0194

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 03 Nov 2028 11:20:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: MSA redlines and jurisdiction concerns

Thanks Laura. Two operational points to consider before we send the redline to Elena:

1) Support model: if Storm can seek injunctive relief in NY courts, we need a clause that limits service of process and emergency discovery obligations to protect our infra team from ad hoc subpoenas — suggest language that requires Storm to provide notice to Redwood's legal ops and gives Redwood a short window (48 hours) to seek relief or respond unless the court order is ex parte.

2) Cloud provider subpoenas: add an explicit carve-in that allows us to comply with lawful process directed at the underlying cloud provider (we won't contest those in the interim relief carveout).

Suggested snippet (draft):
"Notwithstanding the parties' agreement to arbitrate, either party may seek provisional injunctive relief in courts located in the claimant's principal place of business for the limited purpose of preventing immediate and irreparable harm; provided, however, that the claimant shall (i) provide prompt written notice to Redwood's legal operations team, and (ii) allow Redwood one business day to seek protective measures in that forum unless the court order is ex parte."

I think that preserves our ops protections and keeps the carveout narrow.

Jonas
Head of Product Partnerships | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 03 Nov 2028 13:45:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: MSA redlines and jurisdiction concerns

Agree with both Laura and Jonas. Commercially, StormCommerce will push for broader wording unless we are explicit. Two quick points:

- Keep the forum tied to "claimant's principal place of business" — Storm can live with NY if that's how we define it, but avoid language like "any court".
- Add a sunset on the carveout where it only applies to interim measures sought prior to arbitration commencement; if arbitration has already begun then the arbitrator should handle injunctive relief unless impracticable.

Proposed final language to send to Elena (combine prior suggestions):

"Notwithstanding the parties' agreement to arbitrate, either party may seek provisional injunctive relief in a court located in the claimant's principal place of business solely to prevent immediate and irreparable harm to person, data, or confidential information. Such relief shall be limited to provisional measures (including temporary restraining orders and preliminary injunctions) and shall not constitute a waiver of the parties' obligation to submit the underlying dispute to arbitration. The claimant shall provide prompt written notice to Redwood's legal operations team and permit Redwood one business day to respond unless the court grants relief ex parte. This carveout does not permit claims for damages to be litigated in court and expires once arbitration on the underlying dispute is commenced, except to the extent necessary to enforce or maintain provisional relief previously obtained."

Send this to Elena unless either of you want further tweaks.

Marissa Cole
VP, Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@stormcommerce.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 03 Nov 2028 16:03:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: MSA redlines and jurisdiction concerns

Elena —

Appreciate the quick turnaround. Based on our internal alignment above, Redwood can accept the compromise set out below and has attached a redlined MSA with the proposed language. Key points:

- Governing law remains Delaware.
- Narrow interim relief carveout: claimant may seek provisional injunctive relief in a court located in the claimant's principal place of business (e.g., New York for StormCommerce) solely to prevent immediate and irreparable harm to person, data, or confidential information.
- Relief is limited to provisional measures (TROs, preliminary injunctions). It does not permit damages litigation in court and does not waive arbitration of the underlying dispute.
- Operational protections: claimant must provide prompt written notice to Redwood's legal operations team and allow Redwood one business day to seek protections or respond unless the court grants ex parte relief.
- The carveout expires once arbitration is commenced, except to the extent necessary to maintain previously obtained provisional relief.

Attached: StormCommerce_MSA_redlines_20281102.pdf (redline with the proposed language implemented) and a short comparison workbook (draft_orderform_comparison.xlsx) showing where Order Form references arbitration versus court exceptions.

If Storm agrees, please confirm and we will incorporate the same approach into the Order Form language. If you want minor edits to the redline, we can take them now and aim to circulate final MSA for sign-off by end of next week to meet your procurement timeline.

Thanks,

Laura Bennett
